lines.text: Ahn ahn!
UP NEPA!
UP NEPA!
They'll call it off by Friday. My uncle said.
They'll call it off by Friday. My uncle said.
How far? [How are you?]
Guy, you don chop? [Have you eaten?] Don't lie.
Sannu! [Hi!] Long time. Since yesterday.
Let me go and read. By read, I mean sleep near my books.
Look at this one, dressed like results are out.
Ahn ahn! I was on the last paragraph!
Who has a power bank? I'll pay in gratitude and pure water.
UP NEPA!
Light don come! [Power is back!] Plug everything! Everything!
Rain is falling. Half the class has declared a public holiday.
This sun is personal. I didn't offend it.
…and he said 'see me after class'. I've been after class for three days.
Sapa has entered the chat. Sapa is now group admin.
It's giving garri. It's giving garri with no sugar.
Breaking news: he read. The whole night. Nobody knows why.
Network is showing 'E' again. E for 'Eh, sorry'.
My phone, my power bank and my spirit: all on one bar.
Who carried my bucket? My name is on it in three places!
I'm hungry fa. Not small hungry. Lecture hungry.
…so if the lecturer doesn't come in fifteen minutes, we go. That's the law.
Photocopy man has the handout. The lecturer doesn't. That's the system.
She said she'll 'see me later'. Later of which day?
Who's at the noticeboard at this hour? …Never mind.
The cats sit in a circle by the garden. Don't ask me why.
There's an old man in the garden who never seems to sleep. I'm not checking.
Light goes every evening at seven. Like it has a lecture.
Candle sellers are the richest people on campus now.
Somebody saw a goat in The Spot. It ordered before me.
Mall has twenty-four hours light. Our hostel has twenty-four minutes.
Somebody's tapping our line. My fan is turning like it's tired.
Escalator! I've climbed it four times. Bought nothing.
The meter reader came. Nobody had a meter. Everybody had a reader.
Strike, day thirty. I've rearranged my room nine times.
Free class under the tree today. Bring your own shade.
My uncle said they'll call it off by Friday. He's said it for six Fridays.
Sapa combo: garri, groundnut, and good attitude.
The hostel is so empty, I greeted my own echo.
Did you see the video? Don't send it. …Send it.
It's not gossip if three people say it. Then it's research.
Point of order! …Sorry. Election week does this to me.
Everybody is a campaign manager this week. Nobody is a voter.
Somebody said the clock moved. Somebody else said they're lying. Gist.
Project, project, project. I dream in chapter three.
Supervisor said 'see me Monday'. Which Monday? He didn't say.
Is the campus brighter, or am I just going to miss it?
Sign-out sheet: forty signatures. I only know twelve of these offices.
We came as freshers. Now freshers call us 'senior'. When did that happen?
Look at the freshers. So clean. So lost. So many files.
Library seats are finished. People are reading on the stairs.
Breaking news: he read.
The night reader is in the empty theatre again. One lamp. No sound.
Noticeboard crush! Hold my slippers!
I passed! Call my mum! No, call my dad first!
Allowance landed! Market tonight! Debts tomorrow!
Thursday market: best prices, busiest pickpockets. Hold your phone.
Strike or no strike, Mai Shayi Audu is open.
We lost? Don't talk to me until Monday.
Free sachet water with every manifesto. I've finished both.
Gowns everywhere! Aunties with cameras! Somebody hold my jollof!
Iftar at the mosque grounds. Dates, kunu, and everybody smiling.
Carols at the chapel tonight. Even the generator is singing along.
Nobody look at me today. I'm single and I have garri.
The dust is so thick, I waved at a pole for a full minute.
